Beginning with outputs from dada2 (ASV and sample read table) and blastn (custom reference database with CR haplotypes).

Previous processing steps are in `2025-sample-sequencing-run.Rmd`

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# metadata
meta <- read_csv("../data/Metadata_extraction_db_format.csv")
```



```{r read-in-data-outputs-from-dada2}
sample_df <- read_csv("csv_outputs/hapo_20260413_sampleTable.csv") %>%
  dplyr::rename(sample = `...1`)

```

## Sample info

```{r asvs-in-samples}
#tmp <- as.data.frame(st.brief)
#sample_df <- rownames_to_column(tmp, var = "sample")

long_df <- sample_df %>%
  pivot_longer(2:length(sample_df)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(reads = value, ASV = name) %>%
  filter(reads > 0)

# long_df %>%
#   write_csv("csv_outputs/microkit_samples_20260324.csv")

long_df %>%
  filter(reads > 1) %>% # pretty minimal read filter
  ggplot(aes(x = sample, y = reads, fill = ASV)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, size = 6)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0))

```

Use the custom blast database on Sedna to assign haplotypes for these data.

This was a little clunky for some reason...
```{sh, eval=F}
blastn -db hapo_CR -query /home/dbaetscher/workdir/blast/HAPO_eDNA/hapo_20260413_ASV.csv -out CR_2025_results.txt -outfmt 6

```


```{r read-in-the-custom-blast-results}
# read in results
# if the same ASV matches at multiple lengths, select the longest (379 bp)
blast_results <- read_tsv("../data/blast_outputs/CR_2025_results.txt", col_names = F) 
blast_data <- blast_results %>%
  dplyr::rename(ASV = X1, ref_id = X2, perc_id = X3, len = X4, mismatch = X5, gap = X6)

top_hits <- blast_data %>%
  group_by(ASV) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = perc_id, n = 1, with_ties = T) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = len, n = 1, with_ties = T) %>% # take just the longest of identical hits
  mutate(ref_id = ifelse(mismatch > 4, NA, ref_id)) %>% # if the CR matches an ASV with many mismatches, that might be indicative of a novel haplotype.
  unique() # get rid of duplicates introduced by switching high mismatches matches to NAs

```

There are two groups from here:
1) ASVs that match reference CR haplotypes at 100% identity and length
2) ASVs that don't match perfectly.

For each ASV, assign to either group.

```{r evaluate-asvs-with-haplotypes}
# which ASVs match at 100% identity
cr_hits <- top_hits %>%
  filter(perc_id == 100)

# which ASVs match at <100% identity?
asv_assignments <- top_hits %>%
  mutate(ref_id = ifelse(perc_id < 100, NA, ref_id)) %>%
  select(ASV, ref_id) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  unique()

```

```{r color-palette}
library(ggsci)

pal21 <- pal_d3("category20")(14)
#pal21 <- c(pal21, "#000000")  # add a 21st color
```


```{r join-asvs-to-sample-dataframe}
edna_unfiltered_df <- long_df %>%
  left_join(., asv_assignments) %>%
  separate(sample, into = c("sample_id", "replicate"), remove = F) %>%
  left_join(., meta, by = c("sample_id" = "extraction_ID")) %>%
  unite(col = "asv_cr", 4,6, remove = F) 

edna_unfiltered_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = alternative_ID, y = reads, fill = ref_id)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(replicate), cols = vars(sample_type), space = "free", scales = "free") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, angle = 90)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal21,  na.value = "grey90") +
  labs(
        title = "2025 eDNA samples, unfiltered\nCR with 100% matches"
  )
  
ggsave("pdf_outputs/2025_samples_CR_by_sampletype.png", width = 13, height = 5)
```
Only haplotypes that match at 100% identity.


Calculate read proportions and use Kim's threshold of 20% of reads per eDNA sample to include/exclude haplotypes.

```{r}
# look at 20% of reads in each replicate
edna_unfiltered_df %>%
  filter(sample_type == "sample") %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  mutate(read_prop = reads/sum(reads)) %>%
  unite(col = "sampling_loc", c(latitude, longitude)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = alternative_ID, y = read_prop, fill = ref_id)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(replicate), cols = vars(sampling_loc), scales = "free", space = "free") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0.9, vjust = 0.5),
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 5)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 5)),
    strip.text = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  ) +
  labs(
    y = "proportion of sequencing reads",
    x = "sample replictes",
    fill = "haplotype",
    title = "2025 eDNA samples, unfiltered\nCR with 100% matches"
  ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal21, na.value = "grey90") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0))

ggsave("pdf_outputs/2025_samples_proportions.png", width = 10, height = 5)
```
Sample filtering:
1) remove samples with <1000 reads
```{r}
edna_min_depth <- edna_unfiltered_df %>%
  filter(sample_type == "sample") %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  mutate(read_prop = reads/sum(reads)) %>%
  unite(col = "sampling_loc", c(latitude, longitude)) %>%
  filter(sum(reads) > 1000) # 1000 read depth filter per sample

# take a look:
edna_min_depth %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = alternative_ID, y = read_prop, fill = ref_id)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(replicate), cols = vars(sampling_loc), scales = "free", space = "free") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0.9, vjust = 0.5),
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 5)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 5)),
    strip.text = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  ) +
  labs(
    y = "proportion of sequencing reads",
    x = "sample replictes",
    fill = "haplotype",
    title = "2025 eDNA samples, replicates > 1000 reads\nCR with 100% matches"
  ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal21, na.value = "grey90") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0))

ggsave("pdf_outputs/2025_samples_proportions_min_depth.png", width = 10, height = 5)
```


Ok, from there, let's use Kim Parsons's 20% read depth filter - just a coarse look:

```{r 20%-read-depth-filter}

    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 5)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 5)),
    strip.text = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  ) +
  labs(
    y = "proportion of sequencing reads",
    x = "sample replictes",
    fill = "haplotype",
```

Great. There are five ASV sequences to explore in more detail, i.e., how closely do they match existing haplotypes vs. how many mismatches?

First, looking back at the blastn results
```{r}
top_hits %>%
  filter(ASV %in% c("ASV12", "ASV5", "ASV56", "ASV65")) %>%
  arrange(ASV)

```
Each of these ASVs has 1 or 2 mismatches with at least one existing haplotype.


I should look at these in Geneious. 
```{r}
library(Biostrings)

seqs <- readDNAStringSet("csv_outputs/hapo_20260413_ASV.csv", format = "fasta")

# Convert to tibble
fasta_tbl <- tibble(
  id = names(seqs),
  sequence = as.character(seqs)
)

# the ASVs of interest:
fasta_tbl %>%
  filter(id %in% c("ASV12", "ASV5", "ASV56", "ASV65")) %>%
  unique() %>%
  write_csv("csv_outputs/ASVs_wo_haps_20perc.csv")

```


Verifying the sequences and their alignments to the reference haplotypes in Geneious, it's clear that they are distinct. And given that 1-base mismatches separate a number of these haplotypes, it seems reasonable that we could designate these as novel.


```{r}
edna_min_depth %>%
  filter(read_prop > 0.2) %>%
  #filter(is.na(ref_id)) %>%
  mutate(haplo = ifelse(is.na(ref_id), ASV, ref_id)) %>%
   ggplot(aes(x = alternative_ID, y = read_prop, fill = reorder(haplo, -read_prop))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(replicate), cols = vars(sampling_loc), scales = "free", space = "free") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0.9, vjust = 0.5),
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 5)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 5)),
    strip.text = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  ) +
  labs(
    y = "proportion of sequencing reads",
    x = "sample replictes",
    fill = "haplotype",
    title = "2025 eDNA samples, replicates > 1000 reads\nCR with 100% matches, ASVs with 20% of reads"
  ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal21, na.value = "grey90") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0))
  
ggsave("pdf_outputs/2025_samples_all_haplos_20perc.png", width = 10, height = 5)
```

ASV12 and ASV65 have 5 mismatches between the two sequences, suggesting that they are independent haplotypes not caused by amplification or sequencing errors.

ASV5 and ASV56 have 1 mismatch between them: a G-A SNP at position 372.


Look at frequency of occurrence:

```{r freq-of-occurrence}
reps_per_sample <- edna_min_depth %>%
  filter(read_prop > 0.2) %>%
  mutate(haplo = ifelse(is.na(ref_id), ASV, ref_id)) %>%
  # how many replicates passing filter per sampling loc?
  group_by(sampling_loc, replicate) %>%
  tally() %>%
  group_by(sampling_loc) %>%
  summarise(n_reps = sum(n))

edna_min_depth %>%
  filter(read_prop > 0.2) %>%
  mutate(haplo = ifelse(is.na(ref_id), ASV, ref_id)) %>%
  group_by(sampling_loc, haplo) %>%
  add_tally(name = "n") %>%
  left_join(., reps_per_sample) %>% # calculated how many PCR reps post-filtering per sampling location
  mutate(freq_occ = n/n_reps) %>% # out of 6 possible PCR replicates, but we didn't get all six for all samples
  ggplot(aes(x = sampling_loc, y = reorder(haplo, -freq_occ), fill = freq_occ)) +
  geom_tile() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0.9, vjust = 0.5),
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 5)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 5))
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis") +
  labs(
    y = "eDNA haplotypes",
    x = "sampling location",
    fill = "frequency of\n occurrence",
    title = "2025 eDNA samples, 20% read depth filter"
  )

ggsave("pdf_outputs/2025_samples_freq_occur_20perc.png", width = 6, height = 4.5)
```


Overall frequency in the 2025 samples:

```{r}
edna_min_depth %>%
  filter(read_prop > 0.2) %>%
  mutate(haplo = ifelse(is.na(ref_id), ASV, ref_id)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(sampling_loc, haplo) %>%
  unique() %>%
  group_by(haplo) %>%
  tally() %>%
  mutate(freq = n/20) %>% # change this to be based on number of sampling locations -- not the sum 
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(haplo, -freq), y = freq, fill = reorder(haplo, -freq))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 5)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 5)),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "eDNA haplotypes",
    y = "frequency",
    fill = "eDNA haplotypes",
    title = "2025 eDNA samples, 20% read depth filter"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal21, na.value = "grey90") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0))
  

ggsave("pdf_outputs/2025_samples_overall_freq_occur_20perc.png", width = 7, height = 4.5)
```
